The FPGA core's OAM2 address counter was **write-only for a release**. It was a real counter — reset at dots 63, 255 and 339, incremented across the sprite-fetch window, its wrap raising `oam2_overflowed` — and **nothing ever read it**. `$2004`'s post-fetch rest value was a hardcoded `sec_oam[0]`.

Making it observable takes the DUT to **AccuracyCoin 149 of 149** and the co-simulation ladder to **150 of 150, 0 failed**.

## The rule was in the ROM, not on the wiki

AccuracyCoin states it in two sentences its own source carries: the OAM2 address "overflows … on dot 321", and when OAM2 is full the PPU "prevents further increments … frozen at index 0". Read together, the documented *"reads OAM2[0] during 321-340"* is **not a constant** — index 0 is where a **complete** window leaves the counter. An interrupted window stops somewhere else, and that is exactly what `Misaligned OAM2 Address` reads.

The fix is a one-shot at documented dot 321 assigning `sec_oam[oam2_addr_next]`, a combinational next-value view. The view is necessary rather than tidy: `oam_bus` uses the documented-minus-one convention while the counter block uses documented dots, so reading the **register** at that edge yields its pre-320 value — 31 ordinarily — and would put sprite 7's X byte on `$2004` for dots 321-340 of every line of every game. In the ordinary case `31 + 1 = 0`, so every fully rendered scanline is byte-identical.

## Two knobs turned out to be one decision

The increment window goes back to **256**, which v2.6.19 had narrowed to 258 on a review argument whose arithmetic was right and whose conclusion was not: the 33rd candidate is suppressed by `!oam2_overflowed`, so both windows perform 32 increments and differ only in **phase**.

Restoring 256 then broke sprite rendering — **6 of 61,440 pixels** in `sprite-render` and the same 6 in `sprite-mask`, identical bounding box. `oam2_overflowed` is consumed by the four sprite-fetch read sites, so moving the wrap from dot 320 to dot 318 puts it **inside** the fetch, where the live flag forces index 0 for the last sprite. v2.6.19 had also deleted the dot-257 freeze latch, on an argument that rested explicitly on the 258 window.

So **258-without-latch** and **256-with-latch** are two self-consistent packages, and only the second is the hardware's: the oracle pairs 256 with the latch and passes both entries. v2.6.19 passed them **by cancellation**.

Shipped configuration: window 256, latch restored and consumed by sprite fetch, `$2004` reading the live counter through `oam2_addr_next`. Three consumers, two states, each named at the site.

## Thirty-five minutes became thirty seconds

`Misaligned OAM2 Address` is the last catalog row, so the full battery is 134 M cycles — about 35 minutes per attempt — and no sub-test ROM existed. `build_sub_test_rom.py` injects the suite and test indices as plain `LDY`/`LDX` immediates and they survive into the binary: **one byte**, at file offset `0x10B5`, `0x02` → `0x03`. Two independent sources agreed the index was 3 before the patch, and it was validated at `Pass` on frame 82 before use.

That is what made **two** experiments affordable instead of one, and the second is what found the coupled latch.

## A picture gets a gate

`chr_wr` fires constantly in the gated corpus — four of six rung-7 mapper ROMs are CHR-RAM — and **no CHR-RAM ROM's consequence had ever been rendered and compared**. All three framebuffer gates ship CHR-ROM by construction, and the mapper ROMs never enable rendering. That is how v2.6.11's CHR-write defect passed 141 green gates and surfaced only in a hand-run montage.

`mkrom.py` program 53 writes 4 KiB of patterns through `$2007` and renders them, so every pixel it draws is a byte the CPU wrote. Reverting the exact v2.6.11 defect now fails it with **28,191 of 61,440 pixels**. The gate asserts `chr_wr assertions:` is non-zero, because a stimulus that never reaches the path reports a pass about nothing.

## The bitstream, and a pin that finally moved

Ten seeds, each from a **clean database**, all at one pinned build date. All ten close; hold binds on every one of them (0.042–0.113 ns against setup's 0.070–0.645), and **seed 1 takes it outright at +0.113 ns**.

**Seed 3 — the pin this release inherited — is now the worst of the ten**, at +0.042. Carrying it forward would have shipped a factor of **2.7** less binding margin for free. v2.6.19 re-swept and the pin did not move, which reads as ceremony right up until the release where it does.

One claim is weakened by measurement and said so rather than quietly kept: seed 8 did not close on v2.6.19's RTL (−0.008 ns) and was the specific counterexample behind "the distribution is mostly positive, not entirely". On this RTL it closes at +0.405 and all ten pass. The claim stands in principle; its evidence is gone.

`releases/RustyNES_20260918.rbf` ships on both repositories.

- An expired claim in the accuracy gate: `accuracycoin.rs` named a "single remaining failure" while `KNOWN_FAILING` beside it had been empty since v2.6.18.
- **Reported upstream:** `TEST_FrozenOAM2Inc` omits an `INC <ErrorCode` between tests 3 and 4, so both report `$0E` and `Fail(3)` cannot be told from `Fail(4)` — the identical defect upstream already fixed for the neighbouring routine. Filed as `100thCoin/AccuracyCoin#66`.

## Verification

AccuracyCoin **144/144** (RAM decoder) · nestest **0-diff** · co-simulation ladder **150 of 150, 0 failed** · DUT AccuracyCoin **149 of 149** with `$0050 = 0x06` on both sides · `release_anchor_audit` 13/13 · `cosim_manifest_audit` · full workspace suite with `test-roms`. `cargo fmt`, workspace clippy plus the feature-combo runs, rustdoc with warnings denied, and the `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` `no_std` build all clean.

**The emulation core is unchanged** — `git diff v2.6.19..HEAD` over `crates/rustynes-{ppu,cpu,apu,core,mappers,gamedb}` is empty — so 144/144 and nestest 0-diff hold **by construction**, and were re-run anyway.

## Not established here

**No hardware has run any bitstream.** Rung 6 still waits on a DE10-Nano with the SDRAM add-on and a SuperStation One, neither attached to this machine — confirmed by checking rather than assumed.

The dot-257 latch carries a **documented residual**: it is written at exactly one dot, under `rendering && fetch_line`, and cleared only at power-on, so rendering enabled between dots 258 and 320 leaves the four sprite-fetch read sites on a previous scanline's overflow state. No gate in the ladder reaches it — the mask-toggle ROMs move `$2001` around dots 242/256/325/339 and none of those lands in 258..320 — so a fix would be unverifiable, and the plausible fix reintroduces exactly the coupling this release measured. Closing it needs a new stimulus and an oracle run.
